# Annotation reference

Every feature shown here is exercised by the [`example/`](../example) project.
Annotations live in regular Go comments. Two namespaces exist:

- `@SnAPI.<Name>(...)` — declarative metadata (handlers, OpenAPI, etc.).
- `@snapi.<name>` — lifecycle markers (no arguments).

Annotation names are case-insensitive.

---

## API-level metadata

Place these on the **package doc comment** of any file in the project (the
example puts them on `api.go`):

```go
// @SnAPI.Title("Example API")
// @SnAPI.Description("This is an example API generated by SnAPI.")
// @SnAPI.Version("1.0.0")
// @SnAPI.Server("http://localhost:8080", "local development")
// @SnAPI.Server("https://api.example.local", "production")
// @SnAPI.SecurityScheme("bearerAuth", "http", "bearer", "JWT")
package api
```

| Annotation                                          | Purpose                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `@SnAPI.Title(name)`                                | OpenAPI `info.title`                     |
| `@SnAPI.Description(text)`                          | OpenAPI `info.description`               |
| `@SnAPI.Version(version)`                           | OpenAPI `info.version`                   |
| `@SnAPI.Server(url, description)`                   | adds an entry to `servers[]`             |
| `@SnAPI.SecurityScheme(name, type, scheme, format)` | declares a reusable auth scheme          |

---

## Handlers

A handler is any function with the signature
`func(runtime.Request, runtime.Response)`. SnAPI picks it up when its doc
comment includes an HTTP verb annotation.

```go
// @SnAPI.GET("/todo/{id}")
// @SnAPI.Tags("todo")
// @SnAPI.Summary("Get a single todo by id")
// @SnAPI.OperationID("getTodoById")
// @SnAPI.Path("id", "string", "todo identifier")
// @SnAPI.Header("X-Request-Id", "string", "client trace id", "false")
// @SnAPI.Status(200, "OK")
// @SnAPI.Response(200, "application/json", model.Todo)
// @SnAPI.Status(404, "todo not found")
// @SnAPI.UseMiddleware(api.LoggingMiddleware)
func GetTodo(r runtime.Request, w runtime.Response) { ... }
```

### Routing

| Annotation                | Notes                                                        |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `@SnAPI.GET([path])`      | Path defaults to `/` if omitted. Supports `{param}` syntax. |
| `@SnAPI.POST([path])`     |                                                              |
| `@SnAPI.PUT([path])`      |                                                              |
| `@SnAPI.PATCH([path])`    |                                                              |
| `@SnAPI.DELETE([path])`   |                                                              |

### Metadata

| Annotation                       | Description                                 |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `@SnAPI.Summary(text)`           | Short summary line                          |
| `@SnAPI.Description(text)`       | Long description                            |
| `@SnAPI.OperationID(id)`         | OpenAPI `operationId`                       |
| `@SnAPI.Tags(t1, t2, ...)`       | Group operations in the spec                |
| `@SnAPI.Deprecated`              | Mark the operation deprecated               |
| `@SnAPI.Security(schemeName)`    | Require an auth scheme defined at API level |
| `@SnAPI.UseMiddleware(pkg.Name)` | Wrap the handler with a middleware          |

### Request shape

| Annotation                                          | Description                            |
| --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `@SnAPI.Path(name, type, description)`              | Path parameter                         |
| `@SnAPI.Query(name, type, description, required)`   | Query parameter                        |
| `@SnAPI.Header(name, type, description, required)`  | Request header                         |
| `@SnAPI.Cookie(name, type, description, required)`  | Cookie                                 |
| `@SnAPI.Request(mediaType, GoType)`                 | Request body (can repeat for variants) |

### Response shape

| Annotation                                               | Description                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `@SnAPI.Status(code [, description])`                    | Declared response code                    |
| `@SnAPI.Response(code, mediaType, GoType)`               | Response body type (use `[]T` for arrays) |
| `@SnAPI.ResponseHeader(code, name, type, description)`   | Response header for a given status        |

---

## Middleware

Mark a function with `@SnAPI.Middleware` to make it usable in
`@SnAPI.UseMiddleware(...)`. Signature must be
`func(runtime.Request, runtime.Response, runtime.HandlerFunc)`.

```go
// @SnAPI.Middleware
func LoggingMiddleware(r runtime.Request, w runtime.Response, next runtime.HandlerFunc) {
    log.Printf("Received %s request for %s", r.Raw().Method, r.Raw().URL.Path)
    next(r, w)
}
```

---

## Lifecycle hooks

Plain markers, no arguments. Functions can be either `func()` or
`func() error`. Multiple hooks of the same kind are run in declaration order.

```go
// @snapi.setup
func LoadConfig() error { ... }

// @snapi.setup
func Setup() { ... }

// @snapi.teardown
func Teardown() { ... }
```

| Marker            | When it runs                      |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `@snapi.setup`    | before the HTTP server starts     |
| `@snapi.teardown` | after the HTTP server shuts down  |
